Avatar Lab · Fleeced the Ram · Pose Set

Fleeced — the six guide poses

The six guide poses for Fleeced, the ram already shipping as the app icon (D-155). Painted at every size (D-156), each generated singly from one approved hero, and inset to 70% ink width so it sits at the Analyst's scale. Per the mockup-first rule, nothing is translated to code until sign-off. Decisions: ram-decisions.html · every version: ram-versions.html.

Status — no known defects in the pose set
  • thinking — pupil and weak tilt resolved at v4.
  • point — protruding muzzle gone; direction now carried by shifting laces, eyes and brows across the flat football face, so its silhouette matches the other five.
  • Alpha cut and verified on four grounds; @1x/@2x/@3x exported as 256-colour PNG-8, worst sprite 15.6 KB against the 60 KB budget.

2 · The set at true size

96 pt — the bubble, all six. Every expression survives.

44 pt — Team Review, five poses. Expressions collapse — the accepted cost of D-156.

38 pt — entry card, neutral only. Recognition test passes.

3 · Cut-outs on four grounds

Generated on a dark matte, invisible on ink-0 and obvious elsewhere. The first cut flood-filled from the canvas corners and left the enclosed horn-loop holes black — undetectable on ink-0, glaring on a light card. Fixed by matching background colour globally with a minimum-region guard. The two light rows keep that bug visible.

4 · The anchor test

The bubble attaches at BUBBLE_ANCHOR = {x:.5, y:0} — top-centre, which on a ram is between the horns. Pink line is the anchor, drawn at true top-centre with a real bubble and tail.

Control — The Analyst
Two ways to build a trade.

Clean — the tail lands on empty background above the head.

Fleeced — neutral
Two ways to build a trade.

Contested — the horns rise into the anchor strip.

Fleeced — celebrate
Two ways to build a trade.

Worst case — horns highest exactly where the bubble wants to be.

Decided at D2 — the anchor moves off-centre

BUBBLE_ANCHOR becomes per-mascot. Which corner is still open — top-left is likely, since point aims right and would otherwise point into its own bubble.

5 · The flip test

16 spotlight beats mirror point at a left-hand target, so it must aim right by default.
